item.title: Understanding relations: contexts and meanings of psychological work in Residential Child Care Institutions.
item.description: This article aims at taking a look at the psychologist’s role in juvenile community centres. There are different kinds of Residential Child Care Centres and one constant-as to them- is represented by the psychologist, an important and significant figure in all of the centres aiming at taking in minors, at understanding their needs and at identifying and spotting their skills. item.title: Speech, Event, Desire: Psycho-Pedagogical Perspectives about the Symptom
item.description: The symptom, which plays a crucial role in the psychological sciences, in this study will be primarily approached from its ontological status: regarding the human being as a lingual being, the symptom will be seen as speech emerging from the unconscious or a device to be analyzed in its own language, made of rhetorical figures that suspend the arbitrary correlation between signifier and meaning. item.title: Neuropsychodynamic of anxiety
item.description: Anxiety theory is very important in Freudian psychoanalysis, particulary the concept of signal anxiety which is central to unconscious conflict. According to the relational paradigm, anxiety is an interpersonal and affect regulation problem. Through affective neuroscience, Sullivan's interpersonal theory and Fonagy's mentalization theory, it is possible to develop a relational theory of anxiety. item.description: It is possible to be a couple without marriage commitments and even without living together (as happens to LAT couples); the couple can be restricted to the two partners or include wider relationships; one can be a parent without having generated children with natural relationships.
